findings.reason: an implement node dispatched at §2 would find its negative control red-arm passing and either report a blocker or fabricate a refusal; the section should be collapsed to the doccheck/skill text and its negative control retargeted at a check that genuinely fires.
findings.text: §2 is already implemented at the base revision: `dispatch_batch.section_derivation` (reckon/crew/dispatch_batch.py:639-642) supplies `write_paths` only when the section states them, `dispatch_batch.py:815` queues a node with no write paths, `dispatch_sections.py:101` only validates that any declared path resolves, and `_PlanRead.write_paths` (dispatch_batch.py:415-437) returns `[]` rather than refusing when the sentence is absent; the existing test file already exercises a batch entry (test_a_batch_entry_with_no_write_paths_is_queued:125), a section stating none (:140), a queued launch (:156) and a direct dispatch (:191). §2's negative control — "the section refused for naming no write paths" — therefore cannot reproduce, so the section as written would add tests for behaviour that already passes

findings.reason: naming the existing narrowing turns §1 from "add a new exclusive-kind concept" into a two-line delegation and gives the negative control a real target (a source path refused at the write-time audit, not at promotion).
findings.text: the only genuinely unlanded part of §1 is that the write-time audit's `_outside_declared_scope` reports every changed path outside the declared list, while promotion already narrows the same list through `_changed_artifacts_needing_acceptance` (reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py:2967-2970); as written, §1 reads as if no scope narrowing exists anywhere, which invites a node to build a second classifier rather than make the write-time audit delegate to the promotion one

findings.reason: §3 as written can pass its text-only test while silently emptying the code-review neighbourhood derivation and the `model_paths` match, so the section must state what replaces a plan's write-paths sentence as their input.
findings.text: §3's census of what reads a plan section's write-paths sentence is incomplete: besides skills and `prompts.py`, code consumes plan-declared write paths at `plan_review.code_review_paths_from_plan` (:6242, used by `dispatch_admission._health_review_plan_write_paths`:884 and `_health_review_compose_command`:1008), at `dispatch_plan.py:869` (a role default when the node declares none) and at `dispatch_batch.py:415`; a plan whose sections stop naming write paths makes `code_review_paths_from_plan` return `[]` and drops model-path matching (skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md:233), which §3's done-when does not cover

findings.reason: the honest change is text-and-a-test, not new module surface; a wrapper here would be reviewed as surface added for no behaviour.
findings.text: §2's declared source changes add a thin layer over readers that already tolerate an absent sentence (`section_derivation` `if paths:` guard, `_PlanRead.write_paths` returning `[]`, `write_scope_refusal` returning `None` on empty), and the section does not say why `dispatch_batch`'s existing derivation cannot simply be left alone

findings.reason: lying about the current text would only cost the node a wasted edit; the section's real work is in `skills/reckon-build/SKILL.md:149,176` and the sibling skills, so the plan's endpoint is unchanged either way.
findings.text: §3 lists `prompts.py` as a write path, but its scope fence already states the intended rule ("a dispatched node may change any file in its repository that git can reconcile", declared paths as expected, only unmergeable classes sealed); §3 does not justify touching it

findings.reason: the brief must name `runs.py` as the owner to extend, so the node does not fork the exclusivity vocabulary that the fence, the claim and promotion all read.
findings.text: §1's "exclusive kinds" are already owned: `DEFAULT_EXCLUSIVE_PATHS` (:2553), `_SharedWritePaths.exclusive_pattern` (:2645) and `unmergeable_patterns` (:2750) decide exactly the classes §1 lists, and `promotion_scope._changed_artifacts_needing_acceptance` (:603) already applies them; a design that derives its own exclusive-path predicate duplicates this owner

findings.reason: two ordering rules over one queue drift and the verdict becomes untraceable, so the section must say which existing rule it changes rather than adding a parallel one.
findings.text: §4 proposes "offers it first to a waiting review ... before any implement request", but `priorities_first` (:277) already hoists reviews to the head and `role_share_order` (:201) already reserves a `ROLE_SEAT_SHARE_FLOOR` of seats for a waiting review; as written, §4 would add a third rule over the same queue without saying whether it replaces the seat-share floor or supersedes `priorities_first`'s lead scan

findings.reason: an undefined knob is a decision the worker cannot settle, and an unaccounted verdict field is interface surface added without the section saying what it retires; §1 and §2 at least retire a refusal each, §4 retires none.
findings.text: public_definitions 3216, cli_options 550, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 25; §4 adds "a stated critical level" and a verdict field naming which rule gave a request its slot, naming neither where the critical level is configured nor its default, nor what it retires or merges

findings.reason: the section's interface accounting is wrong in the same direction as its negative control, so the author must either find the surface that really fires or drop the section's code claims.
findings.text: §2 adds a new test file and module surface to retire a refusal that, per the census above, the batch and plan paths do not raise; the surface it claims to remove is therefore not the surface it would touch
